english_source_translation: Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer 46: “MOSES ON THE MOUNT RABBI ELAzAR, son of 'Azariah, said: On Friday, || on the 6th of the month, at the sixth hour of the day, Israel received the Commandments. At the ninth hour of the day they returned to their tents, and the Manna was prepared for them for two days, and Israel rested on that Sabbath full of joy as (with) the joy of the festival, because they were worthy to hear the voice of the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is said, "For who is there of all flesh, that hath heard the voice of the living God speaking out of the midst of the fire, as we have, and lived?" (Deut. 5:26).…”

english_source_translation: Chagigah 11b: “with regard to his daughter born from the woman he raped, which is not written explicitly in the Torah. It is forbidden for this man to have sexual relations with this daughter, despite the fact that she is not the daughter of his wife, as he did not marry her mother. As Rava said: Rabbi Yitzḥak bar Avdimi said to me that this halakha is derived by means of a verbal analogy between the term they [hena], an unusual form of this word, written in one context, and the same term, they, written elsewhere. As it is written: “The nakedness of a woman and her daughter…you shall not take…they [hena] are near kinswomen; it is lewdness” (Leviticus 18:17).…”
kisvei_rav_tzadok_parallel_ref: Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 8:3
kisvei_rav_tzadok_parallel: Kisvei Rav Tzadok Parallel — Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 8:3: “And these three correspond to the three vowel-points of the Torah mentioned in the Tikkunim Zohar Chadash, Tikkunim, and I heard its explanation: that the comprehensive scope of the Torah comprises three matters: to act according to the will of the Blessed Name, and according to the legitimate will of every individual not to cause harm to one's fellow, and likewise according to one's own will, not to harm oneself and to seek one's own genuine welfare as well.…” In Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 8:3 (sharing the proof-text Chagigah 11b), Rav Tzadok develops the complementary dimension of this principle, illuminating how Chagigah 11b anchors the inner service of the heart in Sefer HaZikhronot.

(Yadayim 3:5)—for the entire purpose of wisdom and creation is the bond of love between the Holy One, blessed be He, and the Congregation of Israel.” This teaching from the Ishbitz–Radzin school in Sod Yesharim, The Night of Shabbat Chol HaMoed Pesach 14:1 (expounding Song of Songs 5:6) supplies the foundational Chassidic lens through which Rav Tzadok frames Chagigah 11b in Sefer HaZikhronot.

source_reference: Mishneh Torah, Foundations of the Torah 2
english_source_translation: Mishneh Torah, Foundations of the Torah 2: “It is a mitzvah to love and fear this glorious and awesome God, as [Deuteronomy 6:5] states: "And you shall love God, your Lord" and, as [Deuteronomy 6:13] states: "Fear God, your Lord." What is the path [to attain] love and fear of Him? When a person contemplates His wondrous and great deeds and creations and appreciates His infinite wisdom that surpasses all comparison, he will immediately love, praise, and glorify [Him], yearning with tremendous desire to know [God's] great name, as David stated: "My soul thirsts for the Lord, for the living God" [Psalms 42:3].…”
kisvei_rav_tzadok_parallel: Kisvei Rav Tzadok Parallel — Sichat Malakhei HaSharet 4:20: “And they are hinted at in the words of our Sages (Bereishit Rabbah 10:6): Rabbi Simon said: There is no single blade of grass that does not have a constellation (mazal) [etc., other texts reading: "an angel," which is correct; though "mazal" likewise denotes an angel; see Bava Kamma 2b and Rashi; and that which is stated there: "an animal has no mazal," whereas here they taught that even grass has a mazal, is not contradictory; for he certainly does not hold that animal event…” In Sichat Malakhei HaSharet 4:20 (sharing the proof-text Jerusalem Talmud Sheviit 9:1), Rav Tzadok develops the complementary dimension of this principle, illuminating how Mishneh Torah, Foundations of the Torah 2 anchors the inner service of the heart in Sefer HaZikhronot.

english_source_translation: Deuteronomy 4:32–35: “'For ask now of the days that are past, which were before you, since the day that God created man upon the earth, and from the one end of heaven unto the other, whether there has been any such thing as this great thing is, or has been heard like it? Did ever a people hear the voice of God speaking out of the midst of the fire, as you have heard, and live?... Unto you it was shown, that you might know that the Lord He is God; there is none else besides Him.'”

english_source_translation: Chagigah 11b:6-20b:6: “MISHNA: One may not expound the topic of forbidden sexual relations before three or more individuals; nor may one expound the act of Creation and the secrets of the beginning of the world before two or more individuals; nor may one expound by oneself the Design of the Divine Chariot, a mystical teaching with regard to the ways God conducts the world, unless he is wise and understands most matters on his own. The mishna continues in the same vein: Whoever looks at four matters, it would have been better for him had he never entered the world: Anyone who reflects upon what is above the firmament and what is below the earth, what was before Creation, and what will be after the end of the world.…”

He said to him: 'Once you have enthroned Him (amlikhteih) Above and below and toward the four corners of the heaven, you need prolong it no further.'”
kisvei_rav_tzadok_parallel: Kisvei Rav Tzadok Parallel — Takanat HaShavin 10:44: “And Tosafos there brings from Zevachim [5a] “he lay upon his belly [rami a’me’ohi],” and asks that “it was his way” [and what they wrote there, “their way,” is a scribal error; it should read “his way,” for it was only Reish Lakish’s way thus, and we do not find so with others].…” In Takanat HaShavin 10:44 (sharing the proof-text Berakhot 13b), Rav Tzadok develops the complementary dimension of this principle, illuminating how Berakhot 13b anchors the inner service of the heart in Sefer HaZikhronot.

english_source_translation: Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer 11: “THE WORK OF CREATION ON THE SIXTH DAY ON the sixth day (God) brought forth from the earth all kinds of animals, male and female, clean and unclean. By two signs are they declared to be clean: (the signs are) chewing the cud, and dividing the hoof. Three kinds of animals were chosen for the sacrifice of a burnt-offering, namely, the ox, the lamb, and the goat. Every kind of clean animal which is neither Nevelah (i.e. which has not been slaughtered according to the rules of Shechiṭah) nor Ṭerephah (i.e. torn) in the field is permitted to be eaten, except with regard to three parts, namely, the fat, || the blood, and the sinew of the thigh, as it is said, "As the green herb have I given you all" (Gen. 9:3).…”
kisvei_rav_tzadok_parallel: Kisvei Rav Tzadok Parallel — Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:3: “And at the descent of the heavenly fire in Parashat Shemini it is written: "and they fell on their faces" (Leviticus 9:24). And it is known from the Zohar (Korach 178a) that falling on one's face represents self-sacrifice unto death. For initially they saw that they had not yet reached literal "with all your soul" to arouse the fire Above, until they attained it like conversing from behind the fence.…” In Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:3 (sharing the proof-text Song of Songs 5:6), Rav Tzadok develops the complementary dimension of this principle, illuminating how Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer 11 anchors the inner service of the heart in Sefer HaZikhronot.
kisvei_ishbitz_radzin_parallel_ref: Beit Yaakov on Torah, Lech Lecha 23:3
kisvei_ishbitz_radzin_parallel: Kisvei Beis Ishbitz–Radzin Parallel — Beit Yaakov on Torah, Lech Lecha 23:3: “And as we find regarding the Chayyot of the Chariot (Ezekiel 1:9): “they turned not when they went”, and the Patriarchs are themselves the Chariot, as brought in the holy Zohar (Tzav 28b) and the Midrash (Bereishit Rabbah 47:6).…” This teaching from the Ishbitz–Radzin school in Beit Yaakov on Torah, Lech Lecha 23:3 (expounding Shabbat 88b) supplies the foundational Chassidic lens through which Rav Tzadok frames Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer 11 in Sefer HaZikhronot.

english_source_translation: Midrash Tehillim 19: “Primary source background in Midrash Tehillim 19 illuminating Rav Tzadok's teaching in this passage.”
kisvei_rav_tzadok_parallel: Kisvei Rav Tzadok Parallel — Divrei Chalomot 8:1: “On the first night of Chol HaMoed Pesach, they told me in a dream the meaning of what is stated (Tikkunei Zohar 13): "Moses is within, Jacob is without": For the root of Jacob is the attribute of Truth, which is his inner essence; and the outer garment for Truth is the attribute of Wholesomeness (Temimut), through which he was universally recognized: "and Jacob was a wholesome man" [Genesis 25:27].…” In Divrei Chalomot 8:1 (sharing the proof-text Shabbat 88b), Rav Tzadok develops the complementary dimension of this principle, illuminating how Midrash Tehillim 19 anchors the inner service of the heart in Sefer HaZikhronot.
kisvei_ishbitz_radzin_parallel: Kisvei Beis Ishbitz–Radzin Parallel — Beit Yaakov on Torah, Bereshit 1:22: “And as taught in the Gemara (Shabbat 88b), that the entire world was filled with sweet fragrances—which signifies that the universe was sweetened and refined through the sublime light of His absolute unity.” This teaching from the Ishbitz–Radzin school in Beit Yaakov on Torah, Bereshit 1:22 (expounding Shabbat 88b) supplies the foundational Chassidic lens through which Rav Tzadok frames Midrash Tehillim 19 in Sefer HaZikhronot.

english_source_translation: Proverbs 25: “These too are proverbs of Solomon, which the officials of King Hezekiah of Judah copied: It is the glory of God to conceal a matter,And the glory of a king to plumb a matter. Like the heavens in their height, like the earth in its depth,Is the mind of kings—unfathomable. The dross having been separated from the silver,A vessel emerged for the smith. Remove the wicked from the king’s presence,And his throne will be established in justice. Do not exalt yourself in the king’s presence;Do not stand in the place of nobles. For it is better to be told, “Step up here,”Than to be degraded in the presence of the great.Do not let what your eyes have seen Be vented rashly in a quarrel;Think of what it will effect in the end,When your fellow puts you to shame.…”
kisvei_rav_tzadok_parallel: Kisvei Rav Tzadok Parallel — Takanat HaShavin 15:49: “And Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him, was formed from birth in this state from the root of Truth, which is the antithesis of all bodily desires termed "bread of deceit" (Mishlei 23:3) and falsehood, a transient thing that ceases; unlike "the lip of truth shall be established forever" (ibid.…” In Takanat HaShavin 15:49 (sharing the proof-text Shabbat 88b, Song of Songs 5:6), Rav Tzadok develops the complementary dimension of this principle, illuminating how Proverbs 25 anchors the inner service of the heart in Sefer HaZikhronot.
kisvei_ishbitz_radzin_parallel: Kisvei Beis Ishbitz–Radzin Parallel — Sod Yesharim, Rosh Hashanah 44:2: “The word gedulah ('greatness') signifies the expansion of the Divine Will through all the garments of creation, as stated: 'For ask now of the days that are past, which were before you, since the day that God created man upon the earth' (Deuteronomy 4:32)—recognizing the Creator within every boundary of the cosmos.” This teaching from the Ishbitz–Radzin school in Sod Yesharim, Rosh Hashanah 44:2 (expounding Deuteronomy 4:32) supplies the foundational Chassidic lens through which Rav Tzadok frames Proverbs 25 in Sefer HaZikhronot.

english_source_translation: Chagigah 11b: “with regard to his daughter born from the woman he raped, which is not written explicitly in the Torah. It is forbidden for this man to have sexual relations with this daughter, despite the fact that she is not the daughter of his wife, as he did not marry her mother. As Rava said: Rabbi Yitzḥak bar Avdimi said to me that this halakha is derived by means of a verbal analogy between the term they [hena], an unusual form of this word, written in one context, and the same term, they, written elsewhere. As it is written: “The nakedness of a woman and her daughter…you shall not take…they [hena] are near kinswomen; it is lewdness” (Leviticus 18:17).…”
kisvei_rav_tzadok_parallel: Kisvei Rav Tzadok Parallel — Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:6: “And behold, these two were the prime vanguard chosen for the priesthood, termed "from his youth," characterized by the boiling fervor of alacrity; and they did not heed the requirement of bearing the yoke by waiting one hour, as the Early Pious used to tarry before their prayer (Berakhot 30b). And "one hour" signifies a single measure of deliberation, which sufficed for the pious who shared the zealous nature of Abraham.…” In Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:6 (sharing the proof-text Deuteronomy 4:32), Rav Tzadok develops the complementary dimension of this principle, illuminating how Chagigah 11b anchors the inner service of the heart in Sefer HaZikhronot.
kisvei_ishbitz_radzin_parallel: Kisvei Beis Ishbitz–Radzin Parallel — Beit Yaakov on Torah, Bereshit 1:22: “And as taught in the Gemara (Shabbat 88b), that the entire world was filled with sweet fragrances—which signifies that the universe was sweetened and refined through the sublime light of His absolute unity.” This teaching from the Ishbitz–Radzin school in Beit Yaakov on Torah, Bereshit 1:22 (expounding Shabbat 88b) supplies the foundational Chassidic lens through which Rav Tzadok frames Chagigah 11b in Sefer HaZikhronot.

english_source_translation: Shabbat 88b: “who proceed wholeheartedly and with integrity, it is written: “The integrity of the upright will guide them” (Proverbs 11:3), whereas about those people who walk in deceit, it is written at the end of the same verse: “And the perverseness of the faithless will destroy them.” Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥamani said that Rabbi Yonatan said: What is the meaning of that which is written: “You have ravished my heart, my sister, my bride; you have ravished my heart with one of your eyes, with one bead of your necklace” (Song of Songs 4:9)? At first when you, the Jewish people, merely accepted the Torah upon yourselves it was with one of your eyes; however, when you actually perform the mitzvot it will be with both of your eyes.…”
kisvei_rav_tzadok_parallel: Kisvei Rav Tzadok Parallel — Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Ner HaMitzvot 2:255: “Therefore the Torah is also called "Understanding" (Binah), for there is a wisdom that stems from the heart as well [and the Torah incorporates everything, as written in the Zohar, Yitro 85a]. And this is what they said in Ta'anit (7a): that Torah is compared to three liquids: water, wine, and milk.…” In Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Ner HaMitzvot 2:255 (sharing the proof-text Chagigah 13a), Rav Tzadok develops the complementary dimension of this principle, illuminating how Shabbat 88b anchors the inner service of the heart in Sefer HaZikhronot.
kisvei_ishbitz_radzin_parallel: Kisvei Beis Ishbitz–Radzin Parallel — Beit Yaakov on Torah, Noach 34:15: “charging them never again to separate themselves from their contemporaries, but to surrender their lives for the preservation of the collective totality;” This teaching from the Ishbitz–Radzin school in Beit Yaakov on Torah, Noach 34:15 supplies the foundational Chassidic lens through which Rav Tzadok frames Shabbat 88b in Sefer HaZikhronot.

english_source_translation: Chagigah 13a: “to the inner houses, where there is only light; that source, according to which He is surrounded by darkness, is referring to the outer houses. And Rav Aḥa bar Ya’akov said: There is one more firmament above these, which is above the heads of the divine creatures, as it is written: “And over the heads of the divine creatures there was the likeness of a firmament, like the color of the terrible ice” (Ezekiel 1:22). The Gemara comments: Until here, you have permission to speak; from this point forward you do not have permission to speak, as it is written in the book of Ben Sira: Seek not things concealed from you, nor search those hidden from you. Reflect on that which is permitted to you; you have no business with secret matters.…”
kisvei_rav_tzadok_parallel: Kisvei Rav Tzadok Parallel — Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:100: “However, Hashem, blessed be He, does not bestow bounty as unearned grace, for He established the world such that everything appears to be earned through reward. And even this divine revelation He does not bestow arbitrarily from Himself, but only when a preceding voice of speech ascended on high, whereby it was rightfully entitled to receive its reward to cleave to the Source of divine vitality; and that spark from Hashem attached to that voice and speech is able to reveal it…” In Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:100 (sharing the proof-text Chagigah 13a), Rav Tzadok develops the complementary dimension of this principle, illuminating how Chagigah 13a anchors the inner service of the heart in Sefer HaZikhronot.
kisvei_ishbitz_radzin_parallel_ref: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Vayetzei 8
kisvei_ishbitz_radzin_parallel: Kisvei Beis Ishbitz–Radzin Parallel — Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Vayetzei 8: “In Parashat Vayetzei, the Mei HaShiloach explains that Jacob's service in the house of Laban consisted of extracting the holy sparks concealed within deception, guarding his mind so that no foreign thought could blemish his attachment to the One God.” This teaching from the Ishbitz–Radzin school in Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Vayetzei 8 (expounding Bava Batra 116a) supplies the foundational Chassidic lens through which Rav Tzadok frames Chagigah 13a in Sefer HaZikhronot.

english_source_translation: Tikkunei Zohar 21a:1-24a:2: “Sixth Tiqun Be-REiShYT Rabbi Shim’on arose, and he said to Elijah: [Var. Elijah!] ‘Elijah! I adjure you by the holy kingdom, She Who has fallen in exile! Take permission not to depart from us! For the Shekhinah and Her host are watching out for you, the ministering angels – of whom it is stated: (Is. 33:7) Behold their mighty-ones are shouting outside, [screaming] outside their chambers: “There is none to receive the prayers of Israel!” Many birds are chirping, in prayers, towards their mother, those that are nesting upon the earth, who are watching out for you! And they are all called ‘birds’, after the name of the bird’s nest, which is Holy Mother, of whom it is stated: (Deut. 22:6) When a bird’s nest will happen to be before you... And upon Her it is stated: (Ps.…”
kisvei_rav_tzadok_parallel: Kisvei Rav Tzadok Parallel — Resisei Layla 54:11: “Therefore we recite the Order of the Avodah to render "the calves of our lips" (Hosea 14:3), for in truth everything is enacted today as well in the Heavens above, and atonement is complete even in outward manifestation in this world, except that it is not in physical deed, but through speech, which is also a revelation, though not as tangibly felt in physical action.…” In Resisei Layla 54:11 (sharing the proof-text Isaiah 32:15), Rav Tzadok develops the complementary dimension of this principle, illuminating how Tikkunei Zohar 21a:1-24a:2 anchors the inner service of the heart in Sefer HaZikhronot.
kisvei_ishbitz_radzin_parallel: Kisvei Beis Ishbitz–Radzin Parallel — Beit Yaakov on Torah, Bereshit 1:1: “In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth: the purpose of all creation is that human beings clarify through free choice that there is no independent power in nature outside the Blessed Creator.” This foundational Ishbitz–Radzin teaching in Beit Yaakov on Torah, Bereshit 1:1 illuminates the Izhbitz-Radzin principle that all natural phenomena are garments for Divine Will underlying Rav Tzadok's thought.

english_source_translation: Tosefta Sotah 12:5: “So long as Elijah had not yet been hidden away, the Holy Spirit (Ruach HaKodesh) was abundant in Israel; once Elijah was hidden away, the Holy Spirit departed from them.”
kisvei_rav_tzadok_parallel: Kisvei Rav Tzadok Parallel — Peri Tzadik, Bereshit 1:7: “And our father Jacob corresponds to the holiness of Shabbat, as stated in Bereishit Rabbah (parashah 11): " 'Abraham, regarding whom the observance of Shabbat is not explicitly recorded, etc.; Jacob, regarding whom the observance of Shabbat is recorded, etc.…” In Peri Tzadik, Bereshit 1:7 (sharing the proof-text Tikkunei Zohar 21a:1), Rav Tzadok develops the complementary dimension of this principle, illuminating how Tosefta Sotah 12:5 anchors the inner service of the heart in Sefer HaZikhronot.
kisvei_ishbitz_radzin_parallel_ref: Beit Yaakov on Torah, Lech Lecha 14:43
kisvei_ishbitz_radzin_parallel: Kisvei Beis Ishbitz–Radzin Parallel — Beit Yaakov on Torah, Lech Lecha 14:43: “And all seven days that the woman counts days of purity protect her son so that the foreskin of his flesh not prosecute against him, for the mother's forbearance in refining herself during these seven days, and as explained (in Parashat Tazria), this protects the son.…” This teaching from the Ishbitz–Radzin school in Beit Yaakov on Torah, Lech Lecha 14:43 supplies the foundational Chassidic lens through which Rav Tzadok frames Tosefta Sotah 12:5 in Sefer HaZikhronot.

english_source_translation: Yalkut Shimoni, Bo §187: “So too you find concerning Baruch ben Neriah that he lamented before the Holy One, blessed be He: 'Woe is me now! for the Lord has added grief to my sorrow' (Jeremiah 45:3)—why was I different from all the other disciples of the prophets? Joshua served Moses, and the Holy Spirit rested upon him; Elisha served Elijah, and the Holy Spirit rested upon him ('And the spirit of Elijah rested on Elisha,' II Kings 2:15)!”
kisvei_rav_tzadok_parallel: Kisvei Rav Tzadok Parallel — Resisei Layla 46:1: “The nature of the shofar is to broaden and amplify a sound: one sounds a low voice into its narrow end. By vibrating the particles of air in the hollow of the shofar, the sound emerges outward as a louder voice through its broad end, as is known to students of nature. It is therefore an intermediary instrument between the one who sounds and the one who hears, enabling the listener to receive in broad expansion what the sounder produces from a constricted place.…” In Resisei Layla 46:1 (sharing the proof-text Tikkunei Zohar 21a:1), Rav Tzadok develops the complementary dimension of this principle, illuminating how Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 187 anchors the inner service of the heart in Sefer HaZikhronot.
kisvei_ishbitz_radzin_parallel: Kisvei Beis Ishbitz–Radzin Parallel — Sod Yesharim, Shabbat HaGadol 9:2: “When Erev Pesach falls on Shabbat, temporal days are elevated to their primordial root (yemei kedem), uniting the historical remembrance of the Exodus with the eternal, unshakeable unity of 'Hear O Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is One.'” This teaching from the Ishbitz–Radzin school in Sod Yesharim, Shabbat HaGadol 9:2 supplies the foundational Chassidic lens through which Rav Tzadok frames Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 187 in Sefer HaZikhronot.

english_source_translation: Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 186:4-225:5: “"This month shall be for you." It shall be turned over to you. R. Yehoshua b. Levi said, "It's like a king who had a horologue. When he looked at it, he would know what time of day it was. When his child grew up, he turned over his horologue to them. So too did the Holy One of Blessing, up until this point, calculate the months and years "by my hand". But from this point onwards, behold I am giving it over into your hands: "This month shall be for you." ...…”
kisvei_rav_tzadok_parallel: Kisvei Rav Tzadok Parallel — Resisei Layla 46:1: “The nature of the shofar is to broaden and amplify a sound: one sounds a low voice into its narrow end. By vibrating the particles of air in the hollow of the shofar, the sound emerges outward as a louder voice through its broad end, as is known to students of nature. It is therefore an intermediary instrument between the one who sounds and the one who hears, enabling the listener to receive in broad expansion what the sounder produces from a constricted place.…” In Resisei Layla 46:1 (sharing the proof-text Tikkunei Zohar 21a:1), Rav Tzadok develops the complementary dimension of this principle, illuminating how Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 186:4-225:5 anchors the inner service of the heart in Sefer HaZikhronot.
kisvei_ishbitz_radzin_parallel: Kisvei Beis Ishbitz–Radzin Parallel — Sod Yesharim, Shabbat HaGadol 9:2: “When Erev Pesach falls on Shabbat, temporal days are elevated to their primordial root (yemei kedem), uniting the historical remembrance of the Exodus with the eternal, unshakeable unity of 'Hear O Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is One.'” This teaching from the Ishbitz–Radzin school in Sod Yesharim, Shabbat HaGadol 9:2 supplies the foundational Chassidic lens through which Rav Tzadok frames Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 186:4-225:5 in Sefer HaZikhronot.

english_source_translation: Chagigah 14b: “Our Sages taught: Four entered the Pardes (Orchard of esoteric wisdom), and they were: Ben Azzai, Ben Zoma, Acher (Elisha ben Avuyah), and Rabbi Akiva. Rabbi Akiva said to them: When you arrive at the stones of pure marble, do not say 'Water, water!' for it is stated: 'He who speaks falsehood shall not be established before My eyes' (Psalms 101:7). Ben Azzai gazed and died... Ben Zoma gazed and was stricken... Acher cut the shoots (kitzetz ba-netiot). Rabbi Akiva entered in peace and departed in peace.”
kisvei_rav_tzadok_parallel: Kisvei Rav Tzadok Parallel — Likkutei Maamarim, On Shimshon 9: “And all four sages likewise entered into the Orchard (Pardes), which is the Garden of Eden of Metatron in the World of Yetzirah, as brought in the Zohar (Part I, 27a) and the Tikkunim: that there stands the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil which inverts from staff to serpent and from serpent to staff, as brought there and in the Tikkunim numerous times.…” In Likkutei Maamarim, On Shimshon 9 (sharing the proof-text Chagigah 14b), Rav Tzadok develops the complementary dimension of this principle, illuminating how Chagigah 14b anchors the inner service of the heart in Sefer HaZikhronot.
kisvei_ishbitz_radzin_parallel_ref: Sod Yesharim, The Eighth Day of Pesach 18:1
kisvei_ishbitz_radzin_parallel: Kisvei Beis Ishbitz–Radzin Parallel — Sod Yesharim, The Eighth Day of Pesach 18:1: “Through the three 'firsts' (rishon), Israel merits the building of the Temple and the revelation of the name of the Messiah—attaining the pure perception of Pardes without confusing the garments of creation with the One Who clothes Himself within them.” This teaching from the Ishbitz–Radzin school in Sod Yesharim, The Eighth Day of Pesach 18:1 (expounding Chagigah 14b) supplies the foundational Chassidic lens through which Rav Tzadok frames Chagigah 14b in Sefer HaZikhronot.

english_source_translation: Chagigah 15a: “'Acher cut the shoots'; concerning him Scripture states: 'Suffer not your mouth to bring your flesh into guilt' (Ecclesiastes 5:5). What did he behold? He beheld Metatron, to whom permission had been granted to sit and write down the merits of Israel. He said: 'It is taught that on High there is neither sitting nor rivalry, neither back nor weariness—perhaps, Heaven forbid, there are two powers (shetei reshuyot)!' They led Metatron forth and struck him with sixty lashes of fire... A Heavenly Voice went forth and proclaimed: 'Return, O backsliding children' (Jeremiah 3:22)—except for Acher!”
kisvei_rav_tzadok_parallel: Kisvei Rav Tzadok Parallel — Takanat HaShavin 5:6: “But love cannot be reached by a person’s effort, for “there is no love except between equals” — and how shall the axe boast over the one who hews with it, to say that it loves him? Only God, in His abounding mercy and kindness, calls Knesses Yisrael “My sister, My perfect one, My twin,” and says “I have loved you,” etc.; and when God loves a person, of itself the person loves Him too, and here the arousal from Above always precedes.…” In Takanat HaShavin 5:6 (sharing the proof-text Isaiah 10:15), Rav Tzadok develops the complementary dimension of this principle, illuminating how Chagigah 15a anchors the inner service of the heart in Sefer HaZikhronot.
kisvei_ishbitz_radzin_parallel_ref: Beit Yaakov on Torah, Lech Lecha 1:5
kisvei_ishbitz_radzin_parallel: Kisvei Beis Ishbitz–Radzin Parallel — Beit Yaakov on Torah, Lech Lecha 1:5: “And this is because on high there is neither back of neck (turning away) nor weariness, as taught in the Talmud (Chagigah 15a), and as written concerning the Holy Chayyot (Ezekiel 1:12): "Whithersoever the spirit was to go, they went; they turned not when they went.…” This teaching from the Ishbitz–Radzin school in Beit Yaakov on Torah, Lech Lecha 1:5 (expounding Chagigah 15a) supplies the foundational Chassidic lens through which Rav Tzadok frames Chagigah 15a in Sefer HaZikhronot.

english_source_translation: Bereshit Rabbah 5: ““God said: Let the water under the heavens be gathered to one place, and let the dry land appear, and it was so” (Genesis 1:9). “God said: Let the water…be gathered [yikavu]” – it is written: “At Your rebuke they fled; at the sound [of Your thunder they rushed away]” (Psalms 104:7). Rabbi Berekhya said in the name of Rabbi Abba bar Ami: Let a set measure be established for the water, as it says: “A plumb line [kav] is used for measurement in building. will be extended over Jerusalem” (Zechariah 1:16). Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said in the name of Rabbi Levi: The Holy One blessed be He said: ‘Let the water eagerly await [yekavu] for Me, for what I am going to do with it in the future.’ This is analogous to a king who built a palace and settled mute people in it.…”
kisvei_rav_tzadok_parallel: Kisvei Rav Tzadok Parallel — Likkutei Maamarim, On Shimshon 16: “And these matters are deep, long, and broad, and elucidated unto the discerning mind; and it is impossible to explain everything, save unto one who has merited and whose eyes Hashem, blessed be He, has illuminated “to behold the pleasantness of Hashem” (Psalms 27:4): how all the workings of man's steps and his strategies, his thought and his will, everything in its entirety is drawn forth from the ultimate truth of the thought and will of Hashem, blessed be He, and man is mer…” In Likkutei Maamarim, On Shimshon 16 (sharing the proof-text Isaiah 10:15), Rav Tzadok develops the complementary dimension of this principle, illuminating how Bereshit Rabbah 5 anchors the inner service of the heart in Sefer HaZikhronot.
kisvei_ishbitz_radzin_parallel_ref: Beit Yaakov on Torah, Lech Lecha 57:5
kisvei_ishbitz_radzin_parallel: Kisvei Beis Ishbitz–Radzin Parallel — Beit Yaakov on Torah, Lech Lecha 57:5: “And “a sixth” is akin to the episode of Joseph's brothers with Joseph, who embodied the mystery of the Covenant in extraordinary fear, while his brothers held slight overconfidence from Hashem's utterance to Avraham “As for Me, behold, My covenant is with you”; therefore they sold Joseph— meaning they alienated that attribute of strict vigilance, and were required to repent over this, suffering intensely from it, until they were compelled to bring up his bones and bury them i…” This teaching from the Ishbitz–Radzin school in Beit Yaakov on Torah, Lech Lecha 57:5 (expounding Bereshit Rabbah 5) supplies the foundational Chassidic lens through which Rav Tzadok frames Bereshit Rabbah 5 in Sefer HaZikhronot.

english_source_translation: Berakhot 32a: “Rabbi Chama bar Chanina said: Were it not for these three verses, the feet of the enemies of Israel [a euphemism for Israel] would have tottered: first, 'Whom I have afflicted' (Micah 4:6); second, 'Behold, as the clay in the potter's hand, so are you in My hand, O house of Israel' (Jeremiah 18:6); third, 'And I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you a heart of flesh' (Ezekiel 36:26). Rav Pappa said: It is derived from here: 'And I will put My spirit within you, and cause you to walk in My statutes' (Ezekiel 36:27).”
kisvei_rav_tzadok_parallel: Kisvei Rav Tzadok Parallel — Likkutei Maamarim, On Shimshon 17: “And there are further profound matters within this, for our Sages of blessed memory said in Shabbat (104a): Kuf denotes 'holy' (kadosh), Reish denotes 'wicked' (rasha); and that is because wickedness resides specifically in the passionate desire and intent for sin; for upon an action devoid of intentional thought one is not punished, for under duress the Merciful One exempts him even from exile; and so regarding idolatry they said in Sanhedrin (61b): he is coerced; and so in …” In Likkutei Maamarim, On Shimshon 17 (sharing the proof-text Genesis 23:15, Genesis 23:16), Rav Tzadok develops the complementary dimension of this principle, illuminating how Berakhot 32a anchors the inner service of the heart in Sefer HaZikhronot.
kisvei_ishbitz_radzin_parallel_ref: Beit Yaakov on Torah, Lech Lecha 47:1
kisvei_ishbitz_radzin_parallel: Kisvei Beis Ishbitz–Radzin Parallel — Beit Yaakov on Torah, Lech Lecha 47:1: ““And Hashem said unto Avram: I am God Almighty (El Shaddai); walk before Me, and be wholehearted” (Genesis 17:1). The concept is: behold there exist holy Names that are distant from human grasp, where man cannot reach through his deeds, as in that which is written (Job 35:7): “If you are righteous, what do you give Him?!” And this Name Shaddai is the One Who inclines Himself unto creatures so that they reach Him through their virtuous deed, and akin to what we find in the hol…” This teaching from the Ishbitz–Radzin school in Beit Yaakov on Torah, Lech Lecha 47:1 (expounding Job 35:7) supplies the foundational Chassidic lens through which Rav Tzadok frames Berakhot 32a in Sefer HaZikhronot.

english_source_translation: Niddah 16b: “Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa expounded: The angel appointed over conception is named Lailah (Night). He takes a drop and presents it before the Holy One, blessed be He, saying: 'Master of the Universe, what shall become of this drop? Strong or weak, wise or foolish, wealthy or poor?' Whereas 'wicked or righteous' he does not state, in accordance with Rabbi Chanina, who said: Everything is in the hands of Heaven except the fear of Heaven, as it is stated: 'And now, Israel, what does the Lord your God ask of you, but to fear the Lord your God' (Deuteronomy 10:12).”
kisvei_rav_tzadok_parallel: Kisvei Rav Tzadok Parallel — Machshavot Charutz 8:1: “The four New Years taught at the beginning of tractate Rosh Hashanah (2a) appear to me to correspond to the four letters of the Name Ehyeh which is the Name associated with Keser [Crown] as is known; and through It they were redeemed from Egypt, as written in Parashat Shemos: "and they shall say to me: What is His name? what shall I say unto them?" (Shemos 3:13), where Hashem initially communicated to him this Name; for that initial redemption was the inception of all subsequ…” In Machshavot Charutz 8:1 (sharing the proof-text Genesis 23:15, Genesis 23:16), Rav Tzadok develops the complementary dimension of this principle, illuminating how Niddah 16b anchors the inner service of the heart in Sefer HaZikhronot.

english_source_translation: Chagigah 13a: “to the inner houses, where there is only light; that source, according to which He is surrounded by darkness, is referring to the outer houses. And Rav Aḥa bar Ya’akov said: There is one more firmament above these, which is above the heads of the divine creatures, as it is written: “And over the heads of the divine creatures there was the likeness of a firmament, like the color of the terrible ice” (Ezekiel 1:22). The Gemara comments: Until here, you have permission to speak; from this point forward you do not have permission to speak, as it is written in the book of Ben Sira: Seek not things concealed from you, nor search those hidden from you. Reflect on that which is permitted to you; you have no business with secret matters.…”
kisvei_rav_tzadok_parallel: Kisvei Rav Tzadok Parallel — Divrei Soferim 36:4: “And these correspond to the three levels of toil mentioned in Sanhedrin [99b] on the verse "Man is born unto toil"—where the Sages ask: "I know not whether he was created for the toil of labor, or for the toil of mouth, or for the toil of Torah...…” In Divrei Soferim 36:4 (sharing the proof-text Chagigah 13a), Rav Tzadok develops the complementary dimension of this principle, illuminating how Chagigah 13a anchors the inner service of the heart in Sefer HaZikhronot.
kisvei_ishbitz_radzin_parallel_ref: Tiferet Yosef, Vayeilech and Shabbat Shuvah 5
kisvei_ishbitz_radzin_parallel: Kisvei Beis Ishbitz–Radzin Parallel — Tiferet Yosef, Vayeilech and Shabbat Shuvah 5: “'Return, O Israel, unto the Lord your God' (Hosea 14:2): 'Great is repentance, for it reaches up to the Throne of Glory' (Yoma 86a)—even when a person's intellect is veiled from the supernal mysteries ('Seek not what is too wondrous for you,' Chagigah 13a), the sincere return of the heart pierces through all screens directly to the Creator.” This teaching from the Ishbitz–Radzin school in Tiferet Yosef, Vayeilech and Shabbat Shuvah 5 (expounding Chagigah 13a) supplies the foundational Chassidic lens through which Rav Tzadok frames Chagigah 13a in Sefer HaZikhronot.

english_source_translation: Responsa of the Rivash (Rabbi Yitzchak bar Sheshet) §157: “Moreover, in the Shemoneh Esreh prayer they direct intention in each blessing toward a specific Sefirah; and all this is exceedingly strange in the eyes of one who is not a Kabbalist like them, who considers this a belief in multiplicity. I already heard one of the philosophers speaking disparagingly of the Kabbalists, saying: 'The Christians believe in a trinity, and the Kabbalists believe in ten!'”

He has not dealt so with any nation" Psalms 147:19–20; Chagigah 13a; meaning: "By the word of Hashem were the heavens made," the World of Asiyah (Action) having been formed through speech, and "He declares His words" denotes channeling those divine spoken words directly into the human heart, wh…” In Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 9:2 (sharing the proof-text Chagigah 13a), Rav Tzadok develops the complementary dimension of this principle, illuminating how Responsa Rivash 157 anchors the inner service of the heart in Sefer HaZikhronot.

english_source_translation: Chagigah 11b:6-20b:6: “MISHNA: One may not expound the topic of forbidden sexual relations before three or more individuals; nor may one expound the act of Creation and the secrets of the beginning of the world before two or more individuals; nor may one expound by oneself the Design of the Divine Chariot, a mystical teaching with regard to the ways God conducts the world, unless he is wise and understands most matters on his own. The mishna continues in the same vein: Whoever looks at four matters, it would have been better for him had he never entered the world: Anyone who reflects upon what is above the firmament and what is below the earth, what was before Creation, and what will be after the end of the world.…”
kisvei_rav_tzadok_parallel_ref: Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Dover Tzedek, Berakhot 1:11
kisvei_rav_tzadok_parallel: Kisvei Rav Tzadok Parallel — Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Dover Tzedek, Berakhot 1:11: “And the Mishnah, which is the Oral Torah standing at the subsequent descending level, comprises six orders, matching the dimensions of every physical body possessing six directions: and these are: "that which is Above" [transcending mortal human intellect, corresponding to Seder Zera'im, titled Emunat (Shabbat 31a), for faith transcends human reason], and "that which is Below" [corresponding to Seder Teharot, which purifies the impure who inhabit the lowest, base rungs, refle…” In Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Dover Tzedek, Berakhot 1:11 (sharing the proof-text Chagigah 11b), Rav Tzadok develops the complementary dimension of this principle, illuminating how Chagigah 11b:6-20b:6 anchors the inner service of the heart in Sefer HaZikhronot.
kisvei_ishbitz_radzin_parallel: Kisvei Beis Ishbitz–Radzin Parallel — Tiferet Yosef, Bereshit 1:1: “The Torah opens with 'In the beginning' to teach that even within the darkness and concealment of this world ('and darkness was upon the face of the deep'), a person who seeks Hashem discovers that the darkness itself is a garment concealing His supernal light.” This foundational Ishbitz–Radzin teaching in Tiferet Yosef, Bereshit 1:1 illuminates finding Divine unity within the concealment of the natural order underlying Rav Tzadok's thought.

english_source_translation: Responsa of the Rivash §157: “Thus I informed you what my teacher, Rabbeinu Nissim (the Ran), of blessed memory, told me privately: that Ramban (Nachmanides) entrenched himself far too deeply in believing in this Kabbalistic matter; therefore I do not entrench myself in that wisdom, since I have not received it from the mouth of a wise Kabbalist. And if I have seen commentaries on the mysteries of Ramban, they too do not reveal the roots of that wisdom, revealing one handbreadth while concealing several, so that one is liable to err therein; therefore I chose to have no dealings with hidden things.”
kisvei_rav_tzadok_parallel: Kisvei Rav Tzadok Parallel — Machshavot Charutz 8:13: “And the revelation of Eliyahu (Gilui Eliyahu) is granted unto one whose inward heart the Blessed Name enlightens in purity from every trace of lust; and before the coming of the great and terrible day of Hashem to judge the nations, He will send unto the Children of Israel the prophet Eliyahu, that he may illuminate their innermost depths in purity from all manner of evil lusts at their very root; for in this domain of unbridled lust lies the primary future judgment of the na…” In Machshavot Charutz 8:13 (sharing the proof-text Shabbat 108a), Rav Tzadok develops the complementary dimension of this principle, illuminating how Responsa Rivash 157 anchors the inner service of the heart in Sefer HaZikhronot.

english_source_translation: Responsa of the Rivash §157: “So it is regarding prayer, which is always directed to the Cause of all causes, except that they direct thought to draw down the flow through the Sefirah corresponding to the matter requested... Yet who brings us into all this complexity? Is it not better to pray simply for the sake of Heaven with intention of the heart, and He knows by which path to fulfill what is requested, as it is written: 'Commit your way unto the Lord, trust also in Him, and He will bring it to pass' (Psalms 37:5)?”
kisvei_rav_tzadok_parallel_ref: Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Dover Tzedek, Berakhot 3:81
kisvei_rav_tzadok_parallel: Kisvei Rav Tzadok Parallel — Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Dover Tzedek, Berakhot 3:81: “And this is "Praiseworthy (ashrei) is he who grows in Torah," matching the root ishur, signifying happiness even in this world, as expounded above on "Praiseworthy are you, and it shall be well with you," that even within the physical experiences of this world he is joyful.…” In Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Dover Tzedek, Berakhot 3:81 (sharing the proof-text Shabbat 108a), Rav Tzadok develops the complementary dimension of this principle, illuminating how Responsa Rivash 157 anchors the inner service of the heart in Sefer HaZikhronot.

english_source_translation: Tevuot Shor (by Rabbi Alexander Sender Schor, Siman 35, s.k. 46): Cites several halakhic traditions received from the Geonim that are not explicitly recorded in the Talmud.
kisvei_rav_tzadok_parallel: Kisvei Rav Tzadok Parallel — Takanat HaShavin 6:67: “Furthermore, there is in this a “praise,” in the manner it is stated [in Shabbos 108a], “the one whom a king killed is [more] praiseworthy (kosher-species animals that died improperly) yet not on the hides of non-kosher animals, with a parable: “[it is comparable] to two men who were sentenced to death by the government [malchus] — one the king himself killed, and one the executioner [ispaklator] killed; which of them is more praiseworthy? Say: the one whom the king killed.…” In Takanat HaShavin 6:67 (sharing the proof-text Shabbat 108a), Rav Tzadok develops the complementary dimension of this principle, illuminating how Tevuot Shor 35:46 anchors the inner service of the heart in Sefer HaZikhronot.
kisvei_ishbitz_radzin_parallel_ref: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Lech Lecha 1
kisvei_ishbitz_radzin_parallel: Kisvei Beis Ishbitz–Radzin Parallel — Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Lech Lecha 1: “'Go for yourself from your land, from your birthplace, and from your father's house' (Genesis 12:1): a person must continually strip away habitual assumptions and natural reliances so as to walk solely by the living illumination of God's word in the present moment.” This foundational Ishbitz–Radzin teaching in Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Lech Lecha 1 illuminates the Mei HaShiloach's teaching on transcending habitual nature through living faith underlying Rav Tzadok's thought.

english_source_translation: Shabbat 108a: “Mar the son of Ravina asked Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: Is it permitted to write tefillin upon the skin of a kosher fish? He replied: 'If Elijah comes and declares!' Why 'If Elijah comes and declares'? Meaning, if Elijah comes and declares whether its natural foul odor ceases or not. Rashi explains: It does not mean that Elijah would decide a halakhic dispute, for regarding halakhic permission and prohibition 'It is not in heaven' (Deuteronomy 30:12); rather, Elijah would merely disclose a factual reality.”

english_source_translation: Berakhot 31a: “He brought a valuable cup worth four hundred zuz and broke it before them and they became sad. The Gemara also relates: Rav Ashi made a wedding feast for his son and he saw the Sages, who were excessively joyous. He brought a cup of extremely valuable white glass and broke it before them, and they became sad. Similarly, the Gemara relates: The Sages said to Rav Hamnuna Zuti at the wedding feast of Mar, son of Ravina: Let the Master sing for us. Since he believed that the merriment had become excessive, he said to them, singing: Woe unto us, for we shall die, woe unto us, for we shall die.…”
kisvei_rav_tzadok_parallel_ref: Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Dover Tzedek, Berakhot 3:14
kisvei_rav_tzadok_parallel: Kisvei Rav Tzadok Parallel — Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Dover Tzedek, Berakhot 3:14: “And the third watch embodies the pillar of Torah, which is likened to milk and the nursing of an infant, as written in Pesachim (112a): "More than the calf wishes to suckle, [the cow desires to nurse]." And when the Gemara mentions both the infant suckling and the woman conversing with her husband, the convergence of both together occurs strictly in the third watch, to the exclusion of earlier watches, where one might occur without the other: an infant awake while the mother …” In Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Dover Tzedek, Berakhot 3:14 (sharing the proof-text Pesachim 112a), Rav Tzadok develops the complementary dimension of this principle, illuminating how Berakhot 31a anchors the inner service of the heart in Sefer HaZikhronot.

english_source_translation: Berakhot 28b: “After mentioning until when the additional prayer may be recited, the Gemara relates: Rav Avya was ill and did not come to Rav Yosef’s Shabbat lecture. When Rav Avya came the following day, Abaye sought to placate Rav Yosef, and through a series of questions and answers sought to make clear to him that Rav Avya’s failure to attend the lecture was not a display of contempt for Rav Yosef. To this end, he asked him: Why did the Master not attend the Shabbat lecture? Rav Avya said to him: Because my heart was faint and I was unable to attend. Abaye said to him: Why did you not eat something and come? Rav Avya said to him: Does the Master not hold in accordance with that statement of Rav Huna? As Rav Huna said: A person may not taste anything before he recites the additional prayer.…”
kisvei_rav_tzadok_parallel: Kisvei Rav Tzadok Parallel — Machshavot Charutz 9:1: “There are four mitzvos of eating on the night of Pesach: the Passover offering, Matzah, Maror, and the Four Cups, drinking being subsumed under eating (Pesachim 114b); and the collective of these eating mitzvos appears to me to correspond to the Divine Name of Adonut (Aleph-Dalet-Nun-Yud = 65), whose acronym equals that very Name with the kollel; and this is the Divine Name dwelling within and amidst the Children of Israel; and through this their physical eating can likewise …” In Machshavot Charutz 9:1 (sharing the proof-text Pesachim 112a), Rav Tzadok develops the complementary dimension of this principle, illuminating how Berakhot 28b anchors the inner service of the heart in Sefer HaZikhronot.

english_source_translation: Pesachim 112a: “One who lets blood and does not wash his hands will be afraid for seven days. One who cuts his hair and does not wash his hands will be afraid for three days. One who cuts his nails and does not wash his hands will be afraid for one day, and he will not know what is frightening him. Placing one’s hand on his nostrils is a way to become afraid. Placing one’s hand on his forehead is a way to fall asleep. A Sage taught: If food and drink are under one’s bed, even if they are covered with iron vessels, an evil spirit rests upon them. The Sages taught: A person should not drink water on Tuesday nights or on Shabbat nights, i.e., Friday nights. And if he drinks water, his blood is upon his own head, due to the danger.…”
kisvei_rav_tzadok_parallel_ref: Ohr Zarua LaTzadik, Large Beth; Small Beth 8
kisvei_rav_tzadok_parallel: Kisvei Rav Tzadok Parallel — Ohr Zarua LaTzadik, Large Beth; Small Beth 8: “Therefore the Sages stated (Pesachim 112a): More than the calf wishes to suckle, the cow desires to suckle; and so they stated (Kiddushin 2b): Whose way is it to seek after whom? It is the way of a man to pursue a woman; and so they stated (Shabbat 104a): It is the way of the benefactor to pursue the poor. Namely, the generative bestowing force pursues the recipient to channel influx unto it, driven by its active compounding nature.…” In Ohr Zarua LaTzadik, Large Beth; Small Beth 8 (sharing the proof-text Pesachim 112a), Rav Tzadok develops the complementary dimension of this principle, illuminating how Pesachim 112a anchors the inner service of the heart in Sefer HaZikhronot.

english_source_translation: Berakhot 13b: ““Which I command you this day, will be upon your heart.” Surely the word these, does not come to limit the mitzva of intent. On the contrary, from here you derive that the entire portion requires intent. Rabba bar bar Ḥana said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said: The halakha is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Akiva; the entire portion requires intent. Some teach this halakha stated by Rabbi Yoḥanan with regard to that which was taught in a Tosefta, where there is a tannaitic dispute. The first tanna holds: One who recites Shema must focus his heart for the entire Shema. Rabbi Aḥa says in the name of Rabbi Yehuda: Once he focused his heart for the first paragraph alone, he no longer requires intent.…”
kisvei_rav_tzadok_parallel: Kisvei Rav Tzadok Parallel — Tzidkat HaTzadik 183:1: “"Conversing" (sichah) denotes mundane conversation, as written in Sukkah 21b: from the casual conversation of Rabban Gamliel, etc., and in Eruvin 54b on the verse "tell of it, you that walk by the way" (Judges 5:10)—these are the masters of Talmud; but "speech" (dibbur) denotes words of Torah, as written in Ta'anit 10b on the verse "go and speak," see there.…” In Tzidkat HaTzadik 183:1 (sharing the proof-text Berakhot 13b), Rav Tzadok develops the complementary dimension of this principle, illuminating how Berakhot 13b anchors the inner service of the heart in Sefer HaZikhronot.
kisvei_ishbitz_radzin_parallel: Kisvei Beis Ishbitz–Radzin Parallel — Sod Yesharim, Shabbat HaGadol 9:2: “When Erev Pesach falls on Shabbat, temporal days are elevated to their primordial root (yemei kedem), uniting the historical remembrance of the Exodus with the eternal, unshakeable unity of 'Hear O Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is One.'” This teaching from the Ishbitz–Radzin school in Sod Yesharim, Shabbat HaGadol 9:2 (expounding Berakhot 13b) supplies the foundational Chassidic lens through which Rav Tzadok frames Berakhot 13b in Sefer HaZikhronot.

The mishna continues in the same vein: Whoever looks at four matters, it would have been better for him had he never entered the world: Anyone who reflects upon what is above the firmament and what is below the earth, what was before Creation, and what will be after the end of the world.…”
kisvei_rav_tzadok_parallel: Kisvei Rav Tzadok Parallel — Meshiv HaTa'anah, Topic 49 4: “the universal practice follows the equinox of Shmuel; and as the Tosafot Yom Tov wrote in a responsum published in Tzemach Tzedek (sec. 14) that the metaphysical danger is synchronized with Shmuel's equinox, see there. And likewise in chapter Keitzad Me'abrin (Eruvin 56a) concerning Shmuel's statement: 'You have no Nisan equinox falling in Jupiter that does not shatter trees, etc.,' which is computed precisely according to Shmuel's calendar equinox there, see there.…” In Meshiv HaTa'anah, Topic 49 4 (sharing the proof-text Chagigah 11b), Rav Tzadok develops the complementary dimension of this principle, illuminating how Chagigah 11b:6-20b:6 anchors the inner service of the heart in Sefer HaZikhronot.
kisvei_ishbitz_radzin_parallel: Kisvei Beis Ishbitz–Radzin Parallel — Beit Yaakov on Torah, Noach 52:84: “Fulfilling Habakkuk 2:4, 'The righteous shall live by his faith': true life consists of recognizing that all human strength and wisdom flow moment by moment from the Creator alone.” This foundational Ishbitz–Radzin teaching in Beit Yaakov on Torah, Noach 52:84 illuminates living by emunah as the single foundation of all the commandments underlying Rav Tzadok's thought.

english_source_translation: Chagigah 13b: “Rava said: Everything that Ezekiel saw, Isaiah saw. To what may Ezekiel be compared? To a villager who beheld the king [and therefore described the royal chariot in elaborate detail]. And to what may Isaiah be compared? To a townsman who beheld the king [and therefore described the royal court concisely as something familiar].”
kisvei_rav_tzadok_parallel: Kisvei Rav Tzadok Parallel — Peri Tzadik, Lech Lecha 2:3: “''And I will bless you'—the second, corresponding to Yitzchak our Father, peace be upon him, whose attribute was the Fear of Yitzchak, meaning to become refined in the negative prohibitions whose primary root is 'You shall have no other gods,' and this means emptying evil from the heart of folly, so that the evil inclination is purged from there. And this is accomplished via the Oral Torah which represents 'much wisdom' to repair 'much anger.…” In Peri Tzadik, Lech Lecha 2:3 (sharing the proof-text Sefer HaBahir), Rav Tzadok develops the complementary dimension of this principle, illuminating how Chagigah 13b anchors the inner service of the heart in Sefer HaZikhronot.
kisvei_ishbitz_radzin_parallel: Kisvei Beis Ishbitz–Radzin Parallel — Beit Yaakov on Torah, Bereshit 42:24: “and as in the Gemara (Chagigah 13b): “‘Blessed be the glory of the Lord from His place’—and His place no one knows.”” This teaching from the Ishbitz–Radzin school in Beit Yaakov on Torah, Bereshit 42:24 (expounding Chagigah 13b) supplies the foundational Chassidic lens through which Rav Tzadok frames Chagigah 13b in Sefer HaZikhronot.

english_source_translation: Sefer HaBahir: “Rabbi Nechunia ben Hakana said, "One verse states, 'And now men see not the light which is bright in the skies,' (Job 37:21). Another verse states, 'He made darkness His hiding-place' (Psalms 18:12). And it says, 'Clouds and darkness surround Him' (Psalms 97:2). This is a difficulty. A third scripture reconciles them: 'Even the darkness is not too dark for You, But the night shines as the day; the darkness is as the light' (Psalms 139:12)." Rabbi Berechiah said, "It is written, 'Now the earth was tohu and bohu' (Genesis 1:2). What does 'was' mean? That the tohu already was. What is tohu? Something that confounds [m'taha] people. And what is bohu? Tohu was, and it returned to bohu. And what is bohu? A thing that has substance in it, as is written, 'It is inside it [bo hu].…”
kisvei_rav_tzadok_parallel: Kisvei Rav Tzadok Parallel — Ohr Zarua LaTzadik, Introduction 9: “With Heaven's help, concerning the title of this holy book which we named with the title becoming it, Ohr Zaru'a LaTzaddik: my friend, the eminent and pious Rabbi Eliezer Tzvi Ziegelman, may his lamp shine, remarked: it is named after the verse, "but all the children of Israel had light in their dwellings" [Exodus 10:23], since the first treatise in this holy work discusses the exile and Exodus from Egypt, thus far his words.…” In Ohr Zarua LaTzadik, Introduction 9 (sharing the proof-text Sefer HaBahir), Rav Tzadok develops the complementary dimension of this principle, illuminating how Sefer HaBahir anchors the inner service of the heart in Sefer HaZikhronot.
kisvei_ishbitz_radzin_parallel: Kisvei Beis Ishbitz–Radzin Parallel — Tiferet Yosef, Bereshit 7:6: “For these primal forces are immense cosmic forces, as the Talmud states (Chagigah 12a): “Tohu is a green line that encompasses the entire world, etc.,” and regarding Bohu it is taught (Sefer HaBahir): “A thing that has substance”; meaning, the heretic believed there existed an independent cosmic power outside of His divine will, asserting that from Hashem’s pure will alone it were impossible for bounded existence to emerge.” This teaching from the Ishbitz–Radzin school in Tiferet Yosef, Bereshit 7:6 (expounding Sefer HaBahir) supplies the foundational Chassidic lens through which Rav Tzadok frames Sefer HaBahir in Sefer HaZikhronot.

english_source_translation: Bava Batra 12a: “Rabbi Avdimi of Haifa said: From the day the Temple was destroyed, prophecy was taken from the prophets and given to the Sages. Is a Sage then not also a prophet? Rather, he meant: Although prophecy was taken from the prophets, it was not taken from the Sages. Amemar said: And a Sage is greater than a prophet, as it is stated: 'And a prophet has a heart of wisdom' (Psalms 90:12)—who is compared to whom? The lesser is compared to the greater! Ramban and Ritva explain that whereas prophetic vision occurs through the mirror of imagination, the comprehension of the Sages is attained through the illuminated intellect and the Ruach HaKodesh dwelling within them.”
kisvei_rav_tzadok_parallel: Kisvei Rav Tzadok Parallel — Divrei Soferim 38:10: “And our father Isaac, peace be upon him, who embodied this attribute of judgment, had his vision dimmed through Esau's accusations which momentarily found favor in his eyes, rendering him unable to judge by external sight; meriting instead the higher perception of the heart during the blessing, which is the perception of the Tetragrammaton—the rung of Jacob—illuminating before his eyes; matching the declaration: "See, the smell of my son is as the smell of a field which Hashe…” In Divrei Soferim 38:10 (sharing the proof-text Bava Batra 12a), Rav Tzadok develops the complementary dimension of this principle, illuminating how Bava Batra 12a anchors the inner service of the heart in Sefer HaZikhronot.
kisvei_ishbitz_radzin_parallel_ref: Sod Yesharim, The First Day of Pesach 6:1
kisvei_ishbitz_radzin_parallel: Kisvei Beis Ishbitz–Radzin Parallel — Sod Yesharim, The First Day of Pesach 6:1: “'This is the statute (chukat) of the Passover offering' (Exodus 12:43): the statute of Pesach implants the foundational faith of the Exodus into the very nature of the body, which is why the sage's inner grasp of Torah ('a sage is superior to a prophet,' Bava Batra 12a) endures across all generations.” This teaching from the Ishbitz–Radzin school in Sod Yesharim, The First Day of Pesach 6:1 (expounding Bava Batra 12a) supplies the foundational Chassidic lens through which Rav Tzadok frames Bava Batra 12a in Sefer HaZikhronot.

english_source_translation: Sefer Yetzirah 2:3: “Twenty-Two Letters of Foundation—Carved with voice, hewn with spirit, fixed in the mouth in five places: Alef-Heh-Chet-ʽAyin, Bet-Waw-Mem-Peh, Gimel-Yod-Kaf-Qof, Dalet-Tet-Lamed-Nun-Taw, Zayin-Samekh-Shin-Resh-Tzadi. ([In the Mantua printing, the following is added to the paragraph:] Bound to the tongue like a flame to coal—Alef-Chet-Heh-ʽAyin, serving behind the tongue in the house of swallowing. Bet-Waw-Mem-Peh, between the lips and in front of the tongue. Gimel-Yod-Kaf-Qof, being cut upon the third portion of the tongue. Dalet-Tet-Lamed-Nun-Taw, with the tip of the tongue, serving with voice. And Samekh-Tzadi-Resh-Shin, between the teeth and tongue, lain down and flattened.…”
kisvei_rav_tzadok_parallel: Kisvei Rav Tzadok Parallel — Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Ner HaMitzvot 2:171: “And Da'at is Divine Inspiration (Ruach HaKodesh), signifying that Da'at surpasses standard wisdom, as Rashi comments in Shabbat (31a); it is the intuitive wisdom of the kidneys flowing subsequent to the heart's understanding.…” In Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Ner HaMitzvot 2:171 (sharing the proof-text Bava Batra 12a), Rav Tzadok develops the complementary dimension of this principle, illuminating how Sefer Yetzirah 2:3 anchors the inner service of the heart in Sefer HaZikhronot.

kisvei_rav_tzadok_parallel: Kisvei Rav Tzadok Parallel — Peri Tzadik, Lech Lecha 3:8: “And this explains the verse: 'and bundles of myrtle for the groom and the bride': for it aligns with what is taught in the Gemara: 'one for Zakhor and one for Shamor,' and the Ramban in Yitro wrote in the name of Sefer HaBahir, that 'Shamor' is the Sabbath Queen, and 'Zakhor' corresponds to Hashem, blessed be He, and this is 'for the groom and bride.…” In Peri Tzadik, Lech Lecha 3:8 (sharing the proof-text Sefer HaBahir), Rav Tzadok develops the complementary dimension of this principle, illuminating how Sefer HaBahir anchors the inner service of the heart in Sefer HaZikhronot.

english_source_translation: Taanit 9a: ““A tithe shall you tithe [te’aser]” (Deuteronomy 14:22)? This phrase can be interpreted homiletically: Take a tithe [asser] so that you will become wealthy [titasher], in the merit of the mitzva. Rabbi Yoḥanan found the young son of Reish Lakish. He said to the boy: Recite to me your verse, i.e., the verse you studied today in school. The boy said to him: “A tithe shall you tithe.” The boy further said to Rabbi Yoḥanan: But what is the meaning of this phrase: “A tithe shall you tithe”? Rabbi Yoḥanan said to him: The verse means: Take a tithe so that you will become wealthy. The boy said to Rabbi Yoḥanan: From where do you derive that this is so? Rabbi Yoḥanan said to him: Go and test it.…”
kisvei_rav_tzadok_parallel: Kisvei Rav Tzadok Parallel — Kometz HaMinchah 1:41:1: “There in the Midrash Bamidbar Rabbah 1:7: With three things was the Torah given: with fire, with water, and in the wilderness. With fire—alluding to perfection of thought and intense devotion, “see that you are a burning fire” Zohar I, 51a, centered in the heart: “the inclination of man's heart,” dwelling at the two gates of the heart Berakhot 61a, the heart being the broker of contemplation; and with water—alluding to perfection of speech: “My doctrine shall drop as the rain…” In Kometz HaMinchah 1:41:1 (sharing the proof-text Taanit 9a), Rav Tzadok develops the complementary dimension of this principle, illuminating how Taanit 9a anchors the inner service of the heart in Sefer HaZikhronot.
kisvei_ishbitz_radzin_parallel_ref: Beit Yaakov on Torah, Lech Lecha 3:2
kisvei_ishbitz_radzin_parallel: Kisvei Beis Ishbitz–Radzin Parallel — Beit Yaakov on Torah, Lech Lecha 3:2: “And the meaning in this is as brought in Mei HaShiloach: "If you are wise, you are wise for yourself"— meaning, if you arrived at novel Torah insights, 'you are wise for yourself', for all novelty is solely from your perspective, yet to the Torah itself you added no novelty whatsoever, because in truth this too was encompassed in the Torah only that from you it had been concealed until now.…” This teaching from the Ishbitz–Radzin school in Beit Yaakov on Torah, Lech Lecha 3:2 (expounding Taanit 9a) supplies the foundational Chassidic lens through which Rav Tzadok frames Taanit 9a in Sefer HaZikhronot.

english_source_translation: Berakhot 18b: “He was referred to in the verse as son of a living man. The Gemara wonders: Is that to say, the fact that the Bible referred to him with that appellation, that all others are children of the dead? Rather, the verse should be explained as follows: The son of a living man who lives forever, who even in death is referred to as living. Man of Kabze’el who had done mighty deeds, as he accumulated and gathered many workers for the sake of the Torah. Who killed the two lion-hearted men [Ariel] of Moab, as after his death he left no one his equal, in either the First Temple or the Second Temple periods, as the Temple is called Ariel (see Isaiah 29:1), and the two Ariel refers to the two Temples.…”
kisvei_rav_tzadok_parallel_ref: Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 13:5
kisvei_rav_tzadok_parallel: Kisvei Rav Tzadok Parallel — Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 13:5: “And this is the sanctity of Rosh Hashanah: that from the vantage of Hashem, blessed be He, it is strictly one single day; only that our Sages of blessed memory instituted two days, and they constitute one continuous, indivisible sanctity.…” In Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 13:5 (sharing the proof-text Psalms 50:16), Rav Tzadok develops the complementary dimension of this principle, illuminating how Berakhot 18b anchors the inner service of the heart in Sefer HaZikhronot.
kisvei_ishbitz_radzin_parallel: Kisvei Beis Ishbitz–Radzin Parallel — Sod Yesharim, Shemini Atzeret 17:2: “The Holy One, blessed be He, looked into the Torah and created the world, clothing the words of Torah within the garments of creation so that Israel would uncover His unity within every detail of life.” This foundational Ishbitz–Radzin teaching in Sod Yesharim, Shemini Atzeret 17:2 illuminates uncovering the inner light of Torah within the garments of creation underlying Rav Tzadok's thought.

english_source_translation: Psalms 50:16: “And to the wicked, God said:“Who are you to recite My laws,and mouth the terms of My covenant,”
kisvei_rav_tzadok_parallel: Kisvei Rav Tzadok Parallel — Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Ner HaMitzvot 1:14: “(And in Bereishit Rabbah, parashah 1): "'Darkness'—this refers to the deeds of the wicked," etc.: and regarding the wicked Scripture proclaims: "What right have you to declare My statutes?", and "The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination"; and a person cannot bring a gift of mitzvot and good deeds until he first departs from evil.…” In Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Ner HaMitzvot 1:14 (sharing the proof-text Psalms 50:16), Rav Tzadok develops the complementary dimension of this principle, illuminating how Psalms 50:16 anchors the inner service of the heart in Sefer HaZikhronot.
kisvei_ishbitz_radzin_parallel: Kisvei Beis Ishbitz–Radzin Parallel — Beit Yaakov on Torah, Bereshit 1:1: “In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth: the purpose of all creation is that human beings clarify through free choice that there is no independent power in nature outside the Blessed Creator.” This foundational Ishbitz–Radzin teaching in Beit Yaakov on Torah, Bereshit 1:1 illuminates the Izhbitz-Radzin principle that all natural phenomena are garments for Divine Will underlying Rav Tzadok's thought.

english_source_translation: Sanhedrin 99b: “Sing every day, sing every day, i.e., review your studies like a song that one sings over and over. Rav Yitzḥak bar Avudimi says: From what verse is this derived? It is as it is stated: “The hunger of the laborer labors for him; for his mouth presses upon him” (Proverbs 16:26), i.e., he exhausts his mouth through constant review and study. He labors in Torah in this place, this world, and his Torah labors for him in another place, the World-to-Come. Rabbi Elazar says: Every man was created for labor, as it is stated: “Man is born for toil” (Job 5:7). Based on this verse, I do not know whether he was created for toil of the mouth, speech, or whether he was created for the toil of labor.…”
kisvei_rav_tzadok_parallel: Kisvei Rav Tzadok Parallel — Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Ner HaMitzvot 1:14: “(And in Bereishit Rabbah, parashah 1): "'Darkness'—this refers to the deeds of the wicked," etc.: and regarding the wicked Scripture proclaims: "What right have you to declare My statutes?", and "The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination"; and a person cannot bring a gift of mitzvot and good deeds until he first departs from evil.…” In Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Ner HaMitzvot 1:14 (sharing the proof-text Psalms 50:16), Rav Tzadok develops the complementary dimension of this principle, illuminating how Sanhedrin 99b anchors the inner service of the heart in Sefer HaZikhronot.
kisvei_ishbitz_radzin_parallel_ref: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Lech Lecha 1
kisvei_ishbitz_radzin_parallel: Kisvei Beis Ishbitz–Radzin Parallel — Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Lech Lecha 1: “'Go for yourself from your land, from your birthplace, and from your father's house' (Genesis 12:1): a person must continually strip away habitual assumptions and natural reliances so as to walk solely by the living illumination of God's word in the present moment.” This foundational Ishbitz–Radzin teaching in Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Lech Lecha 1 illuminates the Mei HaShiloach's teaching on transcending habitual nature through living faith underlying Rav Tzadok's thought.

english_source_translation: Avodah Zarah 19a: “is referring to our forefather Abraham, who did not walk in the counsel of the members of the generation of the dispersion, who were wicked, as it is stated that they said to each other: “Come, let us build us a city, and a tower, with its top in heaven” (Genesis 11:4), a project with a wicked aim. “Nor stood in the way of sinners” (Psalms 1:1); this too is referring to Abraham, who did not join in the stand of the residents of Sodom, who were sinners, as it is stated: “Now the men of Sodom were wicked and sinners against the Lord exceedingly” (Genesis 13:13). “Nor sat in the seat of the scornful” (Psalms 1:1); this means that Abraham did not sit in the seat of the Philistines, because they were scorners who engaged in jest and buffoonery.…”
kisvei_rav_tzadok_parallel_ref: Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 13:4
kisvei_rav_tzadok_parallel: Kisvei Rav Tzadok Parallel — Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 13:4: “And from the perspective of two visages (du-partzufin), which is Creation from the vantage point of Hashem, blessed be He, there are not two conflicting inclinations; and this is the esoteric mystery of divine Foreknowledge and human Free Will: for from the perspective of this physical world, there is free choice, which is brought about by the deep slumber (tardemah), namely the absence of conscious awareness (da'at), for during sleep, da'at and conscious knowledge depart.…” In Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 13:4 (sharing the proof-text Chagigah 11b), Rav Tzadok develops the complementary dimension of this principle, illuminating how Avodah Zarah 19a anchors the inner service of the heart in Sefer HaZikhronot.
kisvei_ishbitz_radzin_parallel_ref: Tiferet Yosef, Vayeilech and Shabbat Shuvah 5
kisvei_ishbitz_radzin_parallel: Kisvei Beis Ishbitz–Radzin Parallel — Tiferet Yosef, Vayeilech and Shabbat Shuvah 5: “'Return, O Israel, unto the Lord your God' (Hosea 14:2): 'Great is repentance, for it reaches up to the Throne of Glory' (Yoma 86a)—even when a person's intellect is veiled from the supernal mysteries ('Seek not what is too wondrous for you,' Chagigah 13a), the sincere return of the heart pierces through all screens directly to the Creator.” This teaching from the Ishbitz–Radzin school in Tiferet Yosef, Vayeilech and Shabbat Shuvah 5 (expounding Chagigah 13a) supplies the foundational Chassidic lens through which Rav Tzadok frames Avodah Zarah 19a in Sefer HaZikhronot.

english_source_translation: Chagigah 13a: “to the inner houses, where there is only light; that source, according to which He is surrounded by darkness, is referring to the outer houses. And Rav Aḥa bar Ya’akov said: There is one more firmament above these, which is above the heads of the divine creatures, as it is written: “And over the heads of the divine creatures there was the likeness of a firmament, like the color of the terrible ice” (Ezekiel 1:22). The Gemara comments: Until here, you have permission to speak; from this point forward you do not have permission to speak, as it is written in the book of Ben Sira: Seek not things concealed from you, nor search those hidden from you. Reflect on that which is permitted to you; you have no business with secret matters.…”
kisvei_rav_tzadok_parallel_ref: Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Dover Tzedek, Berakhot 1:11
kisvei_rav_tzadok_parallel: Kisvei Rav Tzadok Parallel — Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Dover Tzedek, Berakhot 1:11: “And the Mishnah, which is the Oral Torah standing at the subsequent descending level, comprises six orders, matching the dimensions of every physical body possessing six directions: and these are: "that which is Above" [transcending mortal human intellect, corresponding to Seder Zera'im, titled Emunat (Shabbat 31a), for faith transcends human reason], and "that which is Below" [corresponding to Seder Teharot, which purifies the impure who inhabit the lowest, base rungs, refle…” In Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Dover Tzedek, Berakhot 1:11 (sharing the proof-text Chagigah 11b), Rav Tzadok develops the complementary dimension of this principle, illuminating how Chagigah 13a anchors the inner service of the heart in Sefer HaZikhronot.

kisvei_ishbitz_radzin_parallel: Kisvei Beis Ishbitz–Radzin Parallel — Tiferet Yosef, Vayeilech and Shabbat Shuvah 5: “'Return, O Israel, unto the Lord your God' (Hosea 14:2): 'Great is repentance, for it reaches up to the Throne of Glory' (Yoma 86a)—even when a person's intellect is veiled from the supernal mysteries ('Seek not what is too wondrous for you,' Chagigah 13a), the sincere return of the heart pierces through all screens directly to the Creator.” This teaching from the Ishbitz–Radzin school in Tiferet Yosef, Vayeilech and Shabbat Shuvah 5 (expounding Chagigah 13a) supplies the foundational Chassidic lens through which Rav Tzadok frames Chagigah 13a in Sefer HaZikhronot.

The mishna continues in the same vein: Whoever looks at four matters, it would have been better for him had he never entered the world: Anyone who reflects upon what is above the firmament and what is below the earth, what was before Creation, and what will be after the end of the world.…”

english_source_translation: Chagigah 11b: “with regard to his daughter born from the woman he raped, which is not written explicitly in the Torah. It is forbidden for this man to have sexual relations with this daughter, despite the fact that she is not the daughter of his wife, as he did not marry her mother. As Rava said: Rabbi Yitzḥak bar Avdimi said to me that this halakha is derived by means of a verbal analogy between the term they [hena], an unusual form of this word, written in one context, and the same term, they, written elsewhere. As it is written: “The nakedness of a woman and her daughter…you shall not take…they [hena] are near kinswomen; it is lewdness” (Leviticus 18:17).…”
kisvei_rav_tzadok_parallel: Kisvei Rav Tzadok Parallel — Tzidkat HaTzadik 154:1: “The root of faith (emunah) implanted within every Jewish heart is the experiential recognition that there is no place void of His presence, and even within concealment His providence guides every step.” This parallel in Tzidkat HaTzadik 154:1 directly reinforces Rav Tzadok's exposition here regarding the constant mindfulness of God's unity and providence.

english_source_translation: Zohar, Introduction 12a (Sulam translation): “The fourth commandment is to know that the Lord (YHVH) is Elokim, as it is stated: 'Know therefore this day, and lay it to your heart, that the Lord He is Elokim' (Deuteronomy 4:39)—namely, that the name Elokim (strict judgment and natural law) be included within the name YHVH (mercy), to know that they are One without any division.”
kisvei_rav_tzadok_parallel: Kisvei Rav Tzadok Parallel — Peri Tzadik, Lech Lecha 8:5: “Yet in the holy Zohar (III, 264a) it is taught: ''The Written Torah—that is where Havayah is written; the Oral Torah—where Elohim is written, etc., this is general and this is particular,'' see there; and so wrote in Ra'aya Meheimna (Zohar II, 25a): ''For Hashem He is God'—this is by way of particularization, etc.,' and as written in Tanchuma: Written Torah is generalizations and Oral Torah is details.…” In Peri Tzadik, Lech Lecha 8:5 (sharing the proof-text Zohar, Vaera 4:53), Rav Tzadok develops the complementary dimension of this principle, illuminating how Zohar, Introduction 12a (Sulam) anchors the inner service of the heart in Sefer HaZikhronot.

Jose remarked: ‘But does not the greatest promise of all come last, namely, “I will take you to me for a people and I will be to you a God” (v. 7)?’ R. Judah replied: ‘Deliverance from Egypt was the chief concern of the people then, because they despaired of escaping on account of the magical arts with which the Egyptians held fast their prisoners; hence it came first in order in the proclamation, followed by the promise of deliverance from bondage once and for all, as they might have been afraid that the Egyptians would enslave them again.…”

english_source_translation: Zohar II:25a (Ra'aya Meheimna, Vaera): “'And I will take you to Me for a people, and I will be to you a God; and you shall know that I am the Lord your God' (Exodus 6:7): this commandment is the first of all commandments—to know the Holy One, blessed be He, in a general way (be-khlal), as the supernal Ruler Who created all worlds. Afterwards, at the end of forty years in the wilderness, Moses taught them to know Him in particular detail (be-prat), as it is written: 'Know therefore this day, and lay it to your heart, that the Lord He is Elokim' (Deuteronomy 4:39)—uniting YHVH and Elokim in all the specific mysteries of the Torah.”
